statement: The Volga Bulgaria — a Turkic Muslim trading state controlling the middle Volga fur trade route between the Baltic and the Caspian — was destroyed by the Mongols during the western campaign (1236–1237), several months before the assault on Kievan Rus. Batu Khan's forces sacked the Volga Bulgarian capital (Bulgar/Bilyar) in 1236; the population was massacred or enslaved. The destruction eliminated Islam's most northerly advanced state and the primary intermediary in the Baltic-Caspian fur trade, reshaping the economic geography of the Eurasian steppe.
